Title: Transformation of ALK-positive lung adenocarcinoma to large cell neuroendocrine carcinoma: a case report
PMID: 
Authors: 

Abstract
The transformation of lung adenocarcinoma into large cell neuroendocrine carcinoma (LCNEC) in terms of genotype and histology has been described as a mechanism of acquired resistance to epidermal growth factor receptor tyrosine kinase inhibitor (EGFR-TKI). However, this phenomenon is exceedingly rare in anaplastic lymphoma kinase (ALK)-positive lung adenocarcinoma. Here, we report a case of an ALK-positive lung adenocarcinoma patient who developed resistance following sequential treatment with the ALK-TKI alectinib and lorlatinib, accompanied by histological transformation to LCNEC and concurrent genetic alterations including TP53 deletion, CDKN2A deletion, and MYC amplification. This case expands the spectrum of ALK-TKI resistance mechanisms and highlights the potential value of exploring combinatorial approaches incorporating immunotherapy, antiangiogenic therapy, and chemotherapy for the management of such cases.

Case Reports
An adult patient admitted to Jilin Cancer Hospital with a chief complaint of persistent cough and left-sided limb weakness. Whole-body PET/CT performed on August, 2023, revealed a 6.5 × 4.5 cm mass adjacent to the left lower lobe hilum, accompanied by metastases in the left lower lobe, hilar and mediastinal lymph nodes (stations 1, 2, 4, 5, 7, 8), bone (T10 vertebra and right ilium), and brain (right frontal lobe, 2.0 cm × 2.4 cm; parietal lobe, maximum diameter 1.1 cm) (Fig. 1A). Bronchoscopic biopsy pathology confirmed lung adenocarcinoma (stage cT4N2M1c IVB), and immunohistochemical staining (IHC) showed CK (+), Ki-67 (30% + ), TTF-1 (+), NapsinA (+), P40 (-), CK5/6 (-), and CD8 (+) (Fig. 1B). On September, 2023, next-generation sequencing (NGS) with a 1021-gene panel (GenePlus, Beijing, China) identified an EML4::ALK fusion (2.4%) and EPCAM gene point mutation along with other genomic alterations of uncertain significance (detailed in Table 1) The tumor mutational burden (TMB) was low (0.75 muts/Mb), with microsatellite stable (MSS) status (Table 1) The patient initiated temozolomide for brain metastasis control combined with alectinib on September, 2023. After one month of combination therapy, treatment was transitioned to alectinib monotherapy. Approximately three months into the treatment, follow-up examinations revealed significant tumor regression: the left lung lesion decreased to 2.1×1.1 cm, the right frontal lobe metastasis reduced to 1.0 cm, and the right parietal lobe metastasis shrank to subcentimeter size (<5 mm). The bone metastases as well as the left hilar and mediastinal lymph node metastases remained stable (Fig. 1C) On January, 2024, brain MRI revealed progression of the right parietal lobe metastasis (approximately 1.5 cm in diameter), while other lesions remained stable (Fig. 1D). Therefore, the PFS was only five months. The patient underwent cranial stereotactic radiotherapy (SRT) and continued alectinib therapy. Over the subsequent two months, gradual enlargement was observed in the primary left lung lesion (3.4 × 2.9 cm) and left lower lobe metastasis (Fig. 1E). Consequently, alectinib was discontinued in March 2024 and replaced with lorlatinib. A follow-up scan on July, 2024, demonstrated further enlargement of the left lung lesion (4.8 × 4.0 cm) and slight progression of the right parietal lobe metastasis (0.9 cm) (Fig. 1F). Repeated bronchoscopic biopsy pathological examinations revealed IHC features as follows: vimentin (+), CK5/6 (-), P40 (-), TTF-1 (+), NapsinA (-), CD56 (-), synaptophysin (-), Ki-67 (90% + ), CK ( + ), CK7 (-), CK20 (-), Villin (-), INSM1 (partially +), and PD-L1 (50%+) (Fig. 2A). Combined with morphological characteristics—the tumor cells exhibit a nested growth pattern with organoid structures, the tumor cells are large with abundant cytoplasm and prominent nucleoli—the findings lead to the diagnosis of LCNEC. NGS (1021 panel) confirmed the persistence of the EML4::ALK fusion (35% variant allele frequency) and revealed acquired genomic alterations including TP53 mutation, and copy number gains in MYC and losses in CDKN2A and MTAP, which have been implicated in neuroendocrine differentiation and tumor progression. Other alterations are listed in Table 1. The TMB remained low (7.5 muts/Mb) with MSS status. The presence of wild-type RB1 is more consistent with the NSCLC-like subtype of LCNEC10,11. The patient was then switched from lorlatinib monotherapy to another regimen regarding to toripalimab combined with etoposide and carboplatin. After two cycles, the response was assessed as stable disease (SD). By the fourth cycle, the patient developed thoracic vertebral metastasis-related pain, with slight enlargement of the primary left lung lesion and progression of the right parietal metastasis (1.5 cm), classified as progressive disease (PD) (Fig. 2B). A revised one-cycle regimen of bevacizumab, toripalimab, and nab-paclitaxel was delivered alongside thoracic spine radiotherapy. Symptomatic relief was achieved, and follow-up imaging demonstrated partial response (PR): reduction of the primary left lung lesion to 2.3 × 1.5 cm and the right parietal metastasis to 1.1 cm, with stability at other sites (Fig. 2C). The patient maintained PR after two additional cycles of this regimen and remains under ongoing therapy (Fig. 2D). Fig. 2E showed the patient’s treatment history.
